messages:
alerts-bot: :rotating_light: SLO alert: streaming.p99 latency spiked above 2s (SLO 800ms) for 12m. Affected model: rwd-stream-v2, route: us-west2-prod-stream. Correlated metric: GPU node gpu-23 (host=gpu-23-usw2) reported rising correctable ECC counts and intermittent thermal throttling. Auto-fallback triggered for small fraction of requests.

nisha: seeing the same in dashboard. traces show stalls at step 3/stream token write. p95 still okay, but p99 and p999 tail huge.

tim: I'm oncall — paging in. assigning to myself, will triage. who's owning infra hardware?

maria: infra team, pinging julian. julian, can you confirm gpu health + any recent driver updates?

julian: got it. quick checks: `ssh ops@gpu-23-usw2` then `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL` — output below. looks like multiple Correctable ECC errors over last hour and gpu temp spiked to 92C briefly.

```
GPU 0000:3b:00.0
    ECC Errors:
        Volatile: Single Bit:  12
                 Double Bit:  0
    Temperature
        GPU Current Temp : 92 C
        Thermal Throttle : Active (since 00:10)
```

julian: also grabbed dmesg: `dmesg | tail -n 50` shows repeated ECC corrected messages and occasional GPU hangs that recovered.

mike: customer-ops, any reports from customers?

customer-ops: ACME tenant (acct-acme) reported stalled streams and partial transcriptions failing at ~10:23 UTC. Notified account team, they're seeing degraded UX for a few heavy sessions.

nisha: immediate mitigation plan: 1) route new streaming sessions away from us-west2 for 10m via routing policy; 2) set model fallback for existing streaming requests to rwd-stream-v1-quant if latency persists; 3) drain gpu-23 and cordon node for investigation.

tim: agree. executing now. applying temporary routing -> prefer us-east1/us-west1.

alerts-bot: action: routing policy updated by tim — prefer-region: [us-east1, us-west1]. :white_check_mark:

maria: starting drain: `kubectl drain node/gpu-23-usw2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` — moving pods off. will failover streaming sessions to fallback pool.

julian: while draining, I increased GPU fan curve and lowered power cap to reduce thermal stress: `nvidia-smi -pm 1 && nvidia-smi -pl 200` — monitoring temps. ECC errors still appearing but rate slowed.

mike: rolling deploy of routing change completed. telemetry shows p99 dropping from 2.3s -> 1.1s in last 2min. p95 unchanged. customer-ops updated acct-acme that we mitigated and asked for session IDs for postmortem.

nisha: thanks. next steps: hardware team to inspect gpu card for flaky memory -> possible RMA. infra to collect full ECC dump (`/var/log/nvidia-ecc.log`) and attach to incident. ops to run memtest if possible.

julian: capturing logs and attached to ticket HW-4321. scheduling maintenance window if card needs replacement.

customer-ops: acct-acme confirmed improved UX for new sessions, still recovering a few stuck sessions. they appreciate the quick response.

tim: I'll handoff to night oncall mike in 30m. mike — you'll own follow-up: finalize RMA decision, confirm node remains cordoned, check for kernel/drivers and any pod eviction anomalies.

mike: ack — taking shift. I'll keep monitoring p99 and ECC counts. will escalate to HW oncall if corrected ECCs > 50/hour or if uncorrectable appears.

nisha: adding post-incident checklist: - verify routing policy rollback plan - add synthetic p99 streaming tests in us-west2 to detect thermal regressions - update auto-scaler to pre-warm fallback pool on GPU health anomalies

alerts-bot: incident annotated: severity=high, impacted_customers=[acct-acme], mitigation=region-failover+node-drain, owner=mike.

mike: quick note for postmortem - look into telemetry gap: why auto-fallback wasn't more aggressive earlier. also check if KV cache eviction contributed to stalls during failover.

julian: filing driver/firmware audit task. suspect a recent microcode update on hosts 3/4 might have changed thermal thresholds.

mike: closing active paging for now; will reopen if ECC counts spike. thanks team. :hammer_and_wrench: 

customer-ops: will follow up with ACME next 2 hours with final status.

nisha: tagging this thread for postmortem and assigning to infra+oncall. thanks all for fast coordination. :white_check_mark:
